shared_elements: tall upright pillar/stela with anthropomorphic form (head/upper block above narrower shaft)
low-relief carving covering the front face
horizontal band or belt-like register dividing the surface
animals rendered in profile in relief
curved arm-like elements bent across the body
repeated vertical/hatched linear motifs suggesting fringe or fabric
justification: Both depict a monumental anthropomorphic pillar-figure whose body carries low-relief motifs organised around a horizontal belt-like band with fringed/hatched detailing, with arms bent inward across the torso and animal or creature figures placed on the flanks, plus disc motifs on the chest area. The differences lie in the specifics: A's carvings are largely abstract circles, ovals and looped bands with a broad crescent-shaped element low on the body, while B shows clearly identifiable creatures (a snake-like descending form, quadrupeds and a large bird-like animal in profile) below the belt, so the same general scheme is filled with different specific imagery.
